issues.body: `workflow_triggers` returns `{}` whenever the parsed `on:` value is not a mapping. This is safe for valid shorthand containing only ordinary events, such as `on: push` or `on: [push, pull_request]`, but it also collapses `on: schedule` and `on: [push, schedule]` to the same unscheduled result. Those forms name a scheduled trigger without a readable cron declaration, so silently omitting the lane makes the derived collision map look complete while missing schedule evidence. The self-test blesses `on: push` but does not exercise either schedule-bearing scalar/list form, leaving the prior round's fail-open case intact.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve event names when parsing scalar/list trigger shorthand. Return an unscheduled result for valid shorthand containing only non-schedule events, but raise `CronMapError` whenever a scalar or list contains `schedule`, because no cron list can be derived from that shape. Add hermetic tests proving refusal for both `on: schedule` and a mixed list such as `on: [push, schedule]`, alongside positive tests for `on: push` and `on: [push, pull_request]`.
issues.title: Non-mapping scheduled triggers still disappear from the derived map

verdict.summary: Round 4 extracts the cron derivation into a dedicated module and strengthens malformed mapping-valued `schedule:` handling, but it does not resolve the prior round's remaining parse-boundary failure. `workflow_triggers` still converts every non-mapping `on:` value to `{}`. Consequently malformed schedule-bearing shorthand such as `on: schedule` and `on: [push, schedule]` is indistinguishable from a genuinely unscheduled workflow and disappears from `schedule_minute_map`. The new module's self-test explicitly approves only the harmless scalar `on: push` case and still has no scheduled scalar/list refusal test. The same trust-plane omission remains at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
